summary: Traces how activists from 2003 onward mocked neo-Nazi marches by dressing as clowns, and how by 2019 the far right turned clowns into its own antisemitic Honkler and Clown World memes, spread from 4chan to celebrities and street rallies.

evidence.note: organised protest clowning traced to a UK clown army formed in 2003
2005 clown counter-protest of a neo-Nazi rally in Olympia, Washington
2007 Knoxville clown block; 2012 Charlotte rally follows
Swedish neo-Nazi marches met by clown activists in 2017 and 2018
origin of the Honkler meme on 4chan in early 2019 and its use as a Nazi dog whistle
actor shares a Honkler image traced over the Christchurch shooter
Clown World term found in 2017 far-right chat logs
Proud Boys in clown face at a 2019 Albany rally
Infowars adopts Clown World branding for debate coverage
September 2019 Boston straight pride parade with Honkler costumes

notes: No single bastard; both halves of the episode (clown activism, then the far-right clown memes) share equal weight, so two primary subjects. fascism-far-right chosen as primary over nazism because the meme spread across the wider far right (Proud Boys, Infowars, straight pride); explicitly neo-Nazi groups keep nazism secondary. Finland mentioned only briefly, left out of setting.
